sources.citation: Gedney, William J. 1965. Yay, a Northern Tai language in North Vietnam. Lingua 14:180-193; repr. 1989 in Selected Papers on Comparative Tai Studies (Michigan Papers on South and Southeast Asia 29), 401-414.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Explicitly not investigated: p.403 (repr.) 'a valid phonemic analysis would require a much more thorough investigation, including stress and other features of connected speech, than is needed for comparative Tai studies.' Describes initials, vowels, finals, 6 tones of Yay (Muong Hum / Cha Pa, Lao Cai).

sources.note: Nothing. Ch.1 'Phonology and word list' general remarks cover palatalized/labialized onsets, aspiration, coronal fricatives, finals, obligatory onset, vowel length (only /a/); per-lect phoneme inventories and tones for 24 data points; a full-text search for stress/accent finds no 'stress/accent/unstressed/prominence' anywhere.
